editor_notes.content_quality: Otherwise a dense, well-structured Analysis surveying four AI-claimed complexity-theory/math results this fall (unique games, Aaronson-Ambainis, VP≠VNP, matrix-multiplication exponent), with careful hedging throughout (explicitly notes which claims lack independent human exposition, flags the unreconciled divergence between Anthropic's and OpenAI's VP≠VNP bounds, and separates Aaronson's personal confidence estimate from community consensus). Includes the required Anthropic-maker disclosure sentence.
editor_notes.source_verification: The automated error was independently investigated before accepting it, not taken at face value: re-fetched the flagged URL directly (WebFetch) and got the same HTTP 404, confirming it is not a transient fetch-script issue; also checked the Wayback Machine's availability API for any archived snapshot of this exact URL and found none (empty archived_snapshots), meaning there is no evidence this specific URL ever resolved to real content. This source is cited in the submission for a direct, attributed quote from Imperial College London's Kevin Buzzard ("At the minute, we don't even know why the theorem is true") in the Implications section — a claim that cannot be verified at all while the source is unreachable and unarchived. The other 6 sources (scottaaronson.blog x2, quantamagazine.org, eccc.weizmann.ac.il, github.com/openai x2) were not separately re-verified given the dispositive dead-link finding, per the REJECT path.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Not fully assessable — the Buzzard/Register quote underpinning part of the Implications section cannot be verified against its cited source.
concerns: One of 7 cited sources (theregister.com) is a dead link (HTTP 404), independently reconfirmed via direct fetch and a Wayback Machine check (no archived snapshot exists). It is cited for a direct, attributed quote that is therefore unverifiable. The `sources` array is part of the signed, hashed submission payload and cannot be edited by a reviewer to remove or replace it; per policy, a claim that cannot be traced to a working, verifiable source is not correctable short of a full resubmission.
recommendations: Resubmit with the dead theregister.com source either replaced with a working, verifiable citation for the Buzzard quote, or removed (reframing the Implications section around the remaining, verifiable sources). Note for the allowlist: scottaaronson.blog (Scott Aaronson's own research blog, a recognized complexity-theory authority and primary source for the Aaronson-Ambainis and VP≠VNP claims he is personally reporting on) and eccc.weizmann.ac.il (the Electronic Colloquium on Computational Complexity, a long-established computer-science preprint/technical-report server) both look like legitimate candidates for the allowlist on resubmission, but were not added this review since the submission as a whole is being rejected.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Rejected solely on the unverifiable dead-link source (theregister.com, HTTP 404, no Wayback snapshot) backing a directly attributed quote in the Implications section — confirmed a genuine dead link, not an automated false positive, via independent re-fetch and archive check. The underlying reporting and sourcing methodology elsewhere in the piece (Aaronson's blog, Quanta, ECCC, OpenAI's own repository) is otherwise rigorous, hedged, and well-attributed; recommend the writer resubmit with that one source fixed.
